To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a technique for evaluation of λ(T) and Hc2(T), which is based on magnetization measurements and does not require the use of the Bean model.

the temperature dependences of both the penetration depth and the upper critical field in the YBa2Cu2O7−x system are in good agreement with Ginzbug–Landau predictions, and the value of Tc obtained from low field magnetization data coincides with the temperature at which the upper critical field vanishes.
the superconducting properties, such as penetration depth, coherence length, critical temperature, and critical magnetic field of YBa2 Cu3O7− x ceramics can be determined by magnetization studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of magnetisation data for low density YBCO ceramics.
the evaluation of superconducting parameters of YBa2 Cu3 O7−x samples using the analysis of low field and high field magnetization data.
the magnetization study of the superconducting properties and the determination of the penetration depth λ of the YBa2Cu307−x ceramics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the magnetization measurements of low density YBCO ceramic spheres, carried out at temperatures close to T c in magnetic fields H 0.5 Oe and in magnetic fields H up to 85 kOe, allowed for evaluation of the temperature dependence of both λab (T) and Hc2(T), in agreement with predictions from Ginzburg– Landau theory.
the present analysis of magnetization measurements is applicable to the study of superconductivity of randomly oriented grains of high-temperature superconductors.

the present analysis of magnetization measurements is valid and provides an efficient way of evaluating the temperature dependence of the London penetration depth, the coherence length, and the superconducting transition temperature of superconducting ceramic samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present magnetization study provides an excellent example of the application of the conventional Ginzburg Landau theory to the description of the magnetic properties of YBaCuO ceramics.
magnetization measurements are a powerful tool for investigation of the superconducting properties in low density YBCO ceramics.

the magnetization measurements of YBa2 Cu3O7− x ceramic spheres in magnetic fields up to 85 kOe, in the temperature range of 0.5–85 K, have allowed us to evaluate the superconducting properties, such as the penetration depth, the coherence length, and the upper critical field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analysis of low field magnetization data can provide a wealth of information about the superconducting properties and structure of superconducting samples.
the magnetization measurements in low magnetic fields are a very sensitive tool for evaluation of the superconducting parameters of YBa2CU3O7−X ceramics.

magnetization measurements can be used for evaluation of the temperature dependence of the London penetration depth, the upper critical field, and the coherence length, which are important characteristics of superconducting materials.
